summary.note: One active seam FAILS on a real repository defect: l9-ci-debt-resolver forwards the Authorization header across GitHub's cross-host redirect to blob storage, so job-log acquisition 401s. An earlier revision of this receipt wrongly recorded that as a missing credential and scored the seam partial; the token works and the defect is the resolver's.

failures.summary: transport.py re-sends Authorization across the 302 to productionresultssa4.blob.core.windows.net; Azure returns 401 and the transport maps it to AuthenticationError. Proven by curl -L (200) vs curl -L --location-trusted (401) vs urlopen (401) on the same token and endpoint. With the header stripped at runtime the acquisition completes (93158-byte redacted log, evidence_ready), so this is the sole blocker. Environment-independent: it fails in CI too.
failures.fix: Strip Authorization on cross-host redirect in providers/github/transport.py.

failures.summary: The full producer chain ran, but the corpus (1 record from a real 0-finding SDK bundle) yielded no promotion-eligible candidate, so the publication gate fail-closed. Correct behaviour; the seam is unproven for lack of data.

ingest-review of a REAL review event (l9-ci-core PR #148) got HTTP 403 from api.github.com/graphql. Safety properties were proven with the repo's own example payload; the live review->payload path is unproven.
